population.description: Healthy adults undertaking resistance training, aged 18-70

all.label: trains at least twice a week

gradeRationale.note: Directness is high but the mechanism matters for how we phrase it: the supplement is a convenience vehicle for total intake, not an independent agent. The user-facing explanation must not imply otherwise.

statement: Protein supplementation increases resistance-training-induced gains in lean mass, with the effect driven by reaching an adequate TOTAL daily protein intake rather than by the supplement being superior to food protein.

citations.title: A systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression of the effect of protein supplementation on resistance training-induced gains in muscle mass and strength in healthy adults
International Society of Sports Nutrition Position Stand: protein and exercise
citations.source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

doseResponse.summary: Benefit plateaus at roughly 1.6 g/kg/day of total daily protein; intake beyond that showed no further gain in the meta-regression.
